_meta.indication: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (TANZEUM 30 mg and 50 mg weekly vs placebo)
pivotal_trials.population: Drug-naive adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on diet and exercise
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 52 (albiglutide minus comparator)
pivotal_trials.result: HbA1c change from placebo at Week 52: TANZEUM 30 mg -0.84% (95% CI -1.11, -0.58) and 50 mg -1.04% (95% CI -1.31, -0.77), both p<0.0001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and more than placebo): upper respiratory tract infection (14.2% vs 13.0%), diarrhea (13.1% vs 10.5%), nausea (11.1% vs 9.6%), and injection site reaction (10.5% vs 2.1%)
target_moa: GLP-1 receptor agonist; a recombinant albumin fusion protein that augments glucose-dependent insulin secretion and slows gastric emptying

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF THYROID C-CELL TUMORS — thyroid C-cell tumors observed in rodent studies with GLP-1 receptor agonists; contraindicated in patients with personal or family history of MTC or MEN 2

rems.type: REMS consisting of a communication plan to inform healthcare providers about the serious risks of medullary thyroid carcinoma and acute pancreatitis

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; no new efficacy or safety issue rose to the level of requiring advisory panel input

basis.text: Application was reviewed under Standard review classification

summary.text: Tanzeum (albiglutide) was submitted as a 351(a) BLA with Standard review and received January 14, 2013; it was approved first cycle with a REMS (communication plan) and no advisory committee was convened. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations were granted.

Albiglutide will be approved with a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS), which consists of a communication plan to inform health care providers about the serious risks of thyroid C-cell tumors and pancreatitis.

Albiglutide is the fourth member of the GLP-1 agonist class of anti-diabetic drugs. No new efficacy or safety issue identified in the application rose to the level of requiring the input from an advisory panel. Therefore no advisory committee was convened.
